qa_pairs.instruction: Why does the JDBC driver synchronize garbage strings during synchronization?
qa_pairs.output: The JDBC driver synchronizes garbage strings because the database and the third‑party driver are likely using incompatible character encodings. When the character sets do not match, characters are misinterpreted, resulting in apparent “garbage” data during synchronization.

qa_pairs.instruction: How can you fix garbage string synchronization problems in the JDBC driver?
qa_pairs.output: To resolve garbage string synchronization issues in the JDBC driver, adjust the character encoding used by your third‑party driver so it matches the database encoding. Refer to Sun's list of character encoding values (http://java.sun.com/j2se/1.5.0/docs/guide/intl/encoding.doc.html) and configure the driver to use the appropriate encoding.
